A Laredo Navy veteran who turned to painting to manage post-traumatic stress disorder has seen his work chosen to represent Texas statewide. Hector Leal's painting, titled “Overcoming the Unknown,” won the Texas Governor's Committee on People with Disabilities statewide art contest and was selected for the committee's 2026 Disability Employment Awareness Month poster, according to KGNS.

The painting shows a figure facing the sunrise near El Cenizo. Leal painted the figure in black and gave it a prosthetic leg, a deliberate choice reflecting the idea that a disability does not close off what a person can do. The poster will be distributed to employers across Texas, putting a Laredo artist's work in front of workplaces statewide during Disability Employment Awareness Month.

Leal told KGNS that painting became part of his daily life after his service, and that a fellow veteran pointed him toward free counseling through the VA. He received help through the Laredo Vet Center and the Laredo VA Outpatient Clinic. KGNS cited the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as saying nearly one in four veterans in VA care experience PTSD, a rate higher than in the general population — a reminder, in Leal's story, of why reaching out for help matters, and why a creative outlet can matter too.

Leal hopes the painting reaches other veterans, encouraging them to find an outlet of their own and to keep showing up.

Sources: KGNS, “Laredo veteran's painting selected for statewide disability awareness poster,” Oct. 23, 2026.

title: Laredo veteran's painting chosen for statewide disability awareness poster
